name: Cascadia subduction zone, central Oregon coast segment

fault_trace.comment: APPROXIMATE, hand-digitized reference line, NOT survey-grade. CA GIS (used for SJC/Mojave) is California-only and does not cover Cascadia; no equivalent lightweight open trace service was found for the offshore megathrust in this session. Uses the onshore coastline as a proxy reference line for the locked-zone surface projection (physically defensible: all GNSS stations and crustal seismicity used by this model are onshore, and Cascadia literature routinely references distance-from-coast/deformation-front). 2 anchor points: Newport, OR (44.62,-124.05) to Astoria/mouth of Columbia, OR (46.19,-123.9). Revisit with a real slab-geometry model (e.g. McCrory et al. Slab2) before trusting distance/side calculations here.

gnss.fault_azimuth_comment: approximate, roughly coast-parallel N-S; PCA not available (no polyline_file)

state.v_ref_comment: Cascadia interseismic coupling produces larger coast-normal GNSS signal than a strike-slip corridor -- placeholder pending real calibration against published locking models
state.recurrence_source: The 1700-01-26 Cascadia full-margin M~9 rupture (dated via Japanese tsunami records + coastal subsidence/turbidite paleoseismology) is the last full-margin event -- 326 yr elapsed as of 2026. Recurrence for full-margin ruptures commonly cited ~500-540 yr (turbidite record, Goldfinger et al.), but segment-specific (central vs southern Cascadia) recurrence varies substantially and this figure is NOT sub-segment-specific -- treat as a rough regional anchor, wider uncertainty than either California segment.
